Better Continents world export of "Golden" (seed "GoldenSeed"), 2026-10-04 12:00,
Better Continents <version>, Valheim <game>, sampled on the host.
Every image is 2048 x 2048 pixels over 21000 m (10.259 m per pixel), north at the top.
MAKE A NEW WORLD FROM THIS EXPORT - pick one of the three ways
A. The preset. The export did not make it (switched off); way B makes it.
B. bc_import, for example after you have edited the PNGs.
1. Open the console with F5, in the main menu or in a world.
2. Type   bc_import Golden/export-2026-10-04-12-00-00
(or just  bc_import  for your newest export, or  bc_import list  and then  bc_import <number>).
3. That makes the preset "Golden 2026-10-04 12-00-00" again from the PNGs as they are now and selects it.
Then choose Start, New World, and Create.
C. The config, if you keep editing the PNGs and making worlds from them.
1. Type   bc_import Golden/export-2026-10-04-12-00-00 config   in the console. It copies export.cfg into
BepInEx/config/BetterContinents.cfg (your old file is kept beside it, ending in .before-import-<time>)
and selects the preset "From Config". Or paste export.cfg at the END of that file yourself and save
it: Better Continents reads the file again within a second, with no restart.
2. Every New World you then create with "From Config" reads the PNGs in this folder as they are then.
Setting only Directory in BetterContinents.cfg to this folder works too: a new world made with "From Config"
then also takes the settings in export.cfg, which win over BetterContinents.cfg (edit export.cfg, or delete
it, to use your own). Without them the heights can be read at the wrong scale: export.cfg holds the
Heightmap Amount (2) and Sea Level (0.5) they are encoded for.
A world that already exists keeps the maps it was created with. With the same seed, vegetation, fine lava
detail and the random layout of things come out closest to the exported world.
WHAT EACH FILE IS
heightmap.png     How high the ground is (16-bit grey): black -30 m, white 370 m, the sea (30 m) 0.15.
Only right at Heightmap Amount 2 and Sea Level Adjustment 0.5 (export.cfg sets both).
biomemap.png      Which biome is where, in Better Continents' biome colours (biomemap.txt lists them).
locationmap.png   One dot per location: start temple, bosses, traders, dungeons (locationmap.txt names the colours).
forestmap.png     Forest added to the game's own (16-bit grey): black keeps the game's forest, lighter adds trees.
heatmap.png       The Ashlands heat (16-bit grey): heat = value x 10; Ashlands wherever it is above black.
altbiomemap.png   The alt biomes (Dark Meadows, Wolf Mountain...) exactly as placed (altbiomemap.txt names them).
lavamap.png       Where Ashlands lava is (8-bit grey).
mossmap.png       The Mistlands ground cover (8-bit grey).
paintmap.png      The ground paint of every biome (snow depth and the like), a colour per pixel.
sources/          The loaded world's own Better Continents maps as its settings keep them (not loaded).
export.cfg        The settings that load this folder (way C). It keeps the world's Biome precision (2):
how closely the ground follows the biome map inside each 64 m terrain zone.
manifest.json     Every number about this export, for tools.
Delete a map from the folder, then remake the preset (B), to let the game make that part itself.
EDITING, AND CUTTING AND PASTING BETWEEN EXPORTS
- Edit the PNGs in any image editor. Keep them square PNGs of the same size, and keep heightmap.png,
forestmap.png and heatmap.png 16-bit grey (an 8-bit save turns smooth slopes into steps).
- Two exports line up pixel for pixel when they have the same size, heightmap amount and sea level
(size, heightmapAmount, seaLevel and totalSize in manifest.json). Then an area cut from one pastes into the
same place of the other, and the heights there come out the same.
- Paste the same area from every map (heights, biomes, forest, lava, moss, heat, alt biomes) so they stay
matched, and copy the legend lines (.txt) of any colour the other export's legend lacks.
- Heights are read smoothly, so a seam blends over one pixel; a biome is the one most of the 4 nearest
pixels have.
- A location dot must stay one pixel that touches no other dot of its colour.
- Forest is added to the game's own forest at the new place, so pasted woods keep their extra trees, but the
game's pattern under them changes.
- Only the generated world is exported: buildings, terrain edits and placed objects are not.
THE NUMBERS
Heights: metres = (v x 2 - 0.15 + 0) x 200, v = pixel / 65535.
Past 10000 m the heightmap holds the ground before Better Continents' edge drop-off, which rebuilds the edge.
Pixel (column c, row r) is world x = (c / 2047 - 0.5) x 21000, z = (0.5 - r / 2047) x 21000.
The location map alone uses c / 2048 and r / 2048 (Better Continents' location loader): up to a pixel off the rest.
